security_audit.summary: The executable helper runs caller-supplied commands, including shell-based server startup, so commands require explicit review. Localhost URL findings and most markdown backtick findings are benign examples, but screenshots and console logs can expose sensitive local app data. The skill also contains prompt-injection style guidance that discourages source inspection before running helper scripts.

remediation.suggestion: Avoid shell=True. Accept server commands as argument arrays or restrict execution to reviewed project scripts.
Require explicit user confirmation before running the command after the separator, and document that it executes locally.
Remove the black-box guidance and tell agents to inspect helper scripts before executing them.
Save artifacts only to approved output paths, warn about sensitive data, and redact logs when possible.

content.user_title: Test Local Web Apps with Playwright
content.value_statement: Local web apps need reliable browser checks before release. This skill guides Playwright scripts for screenshots, console logs, selector discovery, and server-backed testing.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to write synchronous Python Playwright scripts for local pages.
Starts one or more local servers before running a browser automation command.
Captures browser console messages and saves them to a log file.
Discovers visible buttons, links, inputs, and page screenshots.
Supports static HTML automation through local file URLs.
Recommends waiting for dynamic pages before inspecting selectors.
limitations: The helper runs local commands supplied by the user, so commands need review before execution.
Examples target localhost and need URL or selector changes for each application.
It does not provide a full test framework or assertions by default.
Screenshots and logs may include sensitive application data.

use_cases.title: Check a Local Feature Flow
use_cases.description: Create a Playwright script that opens a local app, waits for loading, and verifies visible UI behavior.

use_cases.title: Discover Selectors Before Tests
use_cases.description: Inspect rendered buttons, links, and inputs before writing stable test steps.

use_cases.title: Debug Browser Runtime Issues
use_cases.description: Capture screenshots and console messages from a running app to understand UI failures.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Local Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a simple Playwright check for my local app at http://localhost:5173. Wait for the page to load and report the visible controls.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Console Logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to capture browser console messages while I reproduce a UI issue in my local app. Summarize errors and warnings in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Find Stable Selectors
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect the rendered page and identify buttons, links, inputs, and likely stable selectors for a login flow.

prompt_templates.title: Run With Local Servers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a Playwright test for my frontend and backend. Wait for ready ports, then run the workflow after I confirm commands.

output_examples.input: Inspect my local dashboard and list interactive elements.
output_examples.output: The page contains navigation links, dashboard buttons, and form inputs. The report groups each item by role and visible label.

output_examples.input: Capture console output while loading the settings page.
output_examples.output: The result summarizes browser warnings and errors, including when each message appeared during page load.

output_examples.input: Take a screenshot after submitting a static HTML form.
output_examples.output: The output confirms the form interaction and records before-and-after screenshots for visual review.

best_practices: Review server and automation commands before running them.
Wait for dynamic pages to finish loading before capturing state.
Store screenshots and logs in approved paths and remove sensitive files after use.
anti_patterns: Running copied commands from untrusted prompts without inspection.
Assuming localhost examples match production URLs or selectors.
Saving screenshots or console logs that contain secrets.

faq.question: What does this skill help me test?
faq.answer: It helps test local web applications through Python Playwright scripts, screenshots, console logs, and selector inspection.

faq.question: Can it start my development server?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper can start one or more local servers, wait for ports, run a command, and stop the servers.

faq.question: Does it work with static HTML files?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show how to open local HTML files with file URLs and interact with page elements.

faq.question: Does it replace a full test framework?
faq.answer: No. It provides browser automation patterns, but teams still need assertions, fixtures, and reporting for full test suites.

faq.question: What should I review before using it?
faq.answer: Review every local command, server command, output path, screenshot target, and captured log before execution.

faq.question: Can it expose sensitive data?
faq.answer: Yes. Screenshots and console logs may contain tokens, personal data, or internal URLs if the tested app displays them.
